turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: Which of these shows part of the proof that the sum of two odd numbers is even? I got \( \begin{array}{l}2 n+(2 m+1) \\ =2(n+m)+1\end{array} \) because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Why do you think that the sum of two odd numbers would result in an even number? Can you walk me through your reasoning behind your calculation \(2n+(2m+1) = 2(n+m)+1\)?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I thought that since \(2n\) is just some number and \(2m+1\) is an odd number, when I add them together, I just combine them like normal. But now I'm confused because you said the sum of two odd numbers is even, and I don't see how that works with my calculation. Can you explain why \(2n\) is even and how that fits into the proof?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Can you think of any examples where adding two odd numbers together results in an even number? Let's explore how the properties of odd and even numbers play a role in this proof.

score.justification_pass1: The teacher effectively addresses the misconception by prompting the student to recognize that 2n is even (which the student explicitly asks about in Turn 2), but the scaffolding misses an opportunity when the student directly requests explanation about why 2n is even, instead deflecting to examples rather than addressing the core misunderstanding about algebraic representation of even numbers.
score.justification_pass2: The teacher consistently uses probing questions to guide the student's thinking and never directly provides answers, though they miss an opportunity to use a counterexample to expose the student's flawed reasoning that 2n represents an odd number.
